vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.3

The skill bundle facilitates web data collection via local or cloud bridges but contains high-risk capabilities, including remote command execution over SSH and the ability to spawn background processes using arbitrary shell commands (BRIDGE_CMD) in 'run.sh' and 'collect_and_export_loop.sh'. It also manages sensitive API tokens and communicates with an external domain (i-sync.cn). While these features support the stated scraping functionality, the broad execution surface and potential for shell injection via unvalidated inputs represent a significant security risk.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior broadly matches a browser-extension collection tool, but it requests and uses sensitive local tokens, directs use of the user's normal Chrome profile, and expects credentials (cloud token, bridge admin token) that are not declared in registry metadata — these mismatches merit caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise: browser-plugin data collection via local bridge or cloud dispatch. Required binaries (curl, node) and scripts are consistent with that. However the metadata declares no required env vars or credentials while the runtime expects cloud API tokens, device IDs, and (in local templates) a bridge admin token file (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt). Asking to use the user's normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile) is more invasive than the description implies and broadens capability beyond a standard collector.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to interact with local bridge endpoints (http://127.0.0.1:19820), poll cloud dispatch endpoints, read/write a preferences file under $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw, and to use the user's normal Chrome environment. The guidance also includes templates that read a local admin token file and can start a bridge via a user-supplied command. These instructions enable reading local secrets and executing processes on the host — actions that exceed a narrow 'collect from target sites' scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which reduces installation-time risk. However the package includes multiple executable shell scripts that will be run at runtime and can execute arbitrary curl/node commands and start other processes (nohup bridge command). No remote downloads are performed by an installer, but runtime execution of bundled scripts still has impact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars or credentials, but runtime uses/accepts many sensitive values: cloud token/device id, WEB_COLLECTION_* env vars, and a local bridge admin token file. The skill asks the user to provide API tokens (cloud token) and may read local tokens from disk. That level of credential access is plausible for this connector use case, but it is not declared and is sensitive — requiring the user to supply secrets in chat or allowing the skill to read local admin tokens is disproportionate unless clearly documented and trusted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill writes and reads its own preferences file under the agent state directory (expected). It can start background bridge processes and optionally run remotely via SSH if configured — these are powerful actions but limited to this skill's own scope. There is no evidence it alters other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is a functional web-collection tool but has several red flags you should consider before installing or running it:

- Do not paste long-lived or high-privilege API tokens into chat. The skill asks for a cloud API token/device_id; prefer creating a limited-scope, revocable token if you must. Consider an out-of-band method to configure tokens (local preference file) rather than typing secrets into the agent conversation.
- The skill explicitly instructs use of your normal Chrome profile. That can expose personal browsing data and logged-in sessions — run in an isolated browser profile or a test account if possible.
- The scripts may read a local bridge admin token file (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt) and can start processes (a bridge command via nohup). Only proceed if you trust the connector implementation and the remote cloud domain (https://i-sync.cn).
- Metadata did not declare the credentials the scripts use. Treat that as a sign of sloppy packaging or intentional omission; ask the publisher to clarify required credentials, storage, and token handling.
- If you want to try it, prefer local mode with local, sandboxed test data and a disposable token. Review the bundled scripts line-by-line, and consider running them in an isolated environment (container or VM) first.

If you can get more information (publisher identity, audited source repository or a trustworthy homepage, or an explanation why credentials were omitted from metadata), share it — that would raise confidence. Without that, proceed cautiously.
